authorityOverrides.tenantModel: User adjudication over V2.1.2: every Organization concept in this project is Tenant; no Organization compatibility layer
authorityOverrides.iotPlatform: Data Architecture V2: ThingsBoard is removed
authorityOverrides.pointModel: Point is the canonical data point; Sensor exists only for independently identifiable/installable/replaceable/calibratable/traceable physical probes
authorityOverrides.storage: PostgreSQL owns business master/metadata/state machines; ClickHouse owns historical Telemetry/analytics; Redis is rebuildable Latest/current cache; MQTT is transport only; Object Storage owns archive/backup/evidence/dataset/model artifacts
authorityOverrides.identityProvider: User adjudication: Phase 1 uses the platform-owned services/identity-service as Identity Infrastructure. It authenticates credentials and exposes standard OIDC; IAM remains the sole Tenant/Site/Role/Policy authorization authority.
authorityOverrides.edgeControlPlane: User adjudication over V2.1.2 using OpenEMS as an external reference implementation: production controllable HVAC requires a first-class Edge Control Plane with Channel Runtime, Process Image, IPO Cycle, Controller/Scheduler/Arbiter, Capability Profiles, Device Drivers, Protocol Bridges, Edge Manifest, Edge Timedata and leased Cloud Command intents. Cloud retains durable command governance and business-domain authority. Machine contract: contracts/architecture/edge-control-plane.v1.json.

serviceModel.physicalPhase1: energy-api + iot-service + telemetry-worker + metric-worker + supporting scheduler/maintenance workloads + identity infrastructure + selective intelligence services

logicalDomains.reason: Cloud MQTT/S2 runtime is implemented, but the adjudicated target now also requires a first-class HVAC Edge Control Plane with Channel Runtime, Process Image, Cycle, Controller/Scheduler, Capability Profiles, Drivers/Bridges, Edge Manifest and Edge Timedata.
Registry topology structures exist, but released Energy Content ownership, read/mutation contracts and Energy Processing integration are not complete.
The current implementation covers the electricity interval-fact and fixed energy-series slice; it does not yet resolve Registry Meter/MeterBinding semantics or the broader Energy Content boundary.

The Registry boundary is the Phase 1 logical owner for Meter, MeterBinding and Virtual Meter content, but Platform Core currently exposes only Site/Asset/Device routes and the Energy Content contracts are not implemented.

Cloud command governance, dispatch and verification exist, but target execution semantics now require leased Edge intents, local Controller/Scheduler arbitration, reusable safety/interlock controllers and requestedValue/effectiveValue constraint evidence.

crossStorePublication.pattern: PostgreSQL PERSISTING -> ClickHouse by stable run/result identity -> PostgreSQL PERSISTED + durable Outbox; stale PERSISTING is reconciled by proving ClickHouse evidence

physicalPhase1.reason: Phase1 default business deployables remain energy-api + iot-service + telemetry-worker + metric-worker. Scheduler and Maintenance are default supporting application workloads rather than new business-domain deployables: Scheduler owns durable Job coordination, while Maintenance executes privileged cross-domain operational jobs such as credential-expiry scans, dead-work disposition and Tenant retirement. identity-service is separate Identity Infrastructure: it authenticates platform credentials and exposes standard OIDC but owns no Tenant/Site/Role/Policy authorization state. energy-api co-locates Platform Gateway, IAM, Registry Core, Telemetry Query, Audit, Alarm, Work Order and Command while preserving their internal security boundaries; iot-service combines MQTT ingestion with Command dispatch/verification; telemetry-worker owns history and analytics projections; metric-worker owns scheduled Metric finalization and scoped cross-store reconciliation. Forecast, Optimization and FDD remain selective intelligence services behind the optional intelligence profile. Object Storage production capability remains tracked separately.

conformance.reason: SE-API-001 V1.2 CURRENT CANDIDATE remains the common API authority and all 13 reviewed routes are tracked in contracts/architecture/se-api-001-v1.2-runtime-convergence.json. Alarm is fully synchronized and active (A=3). The remaining 10 routes were re-reviewed against SE-DATA-001 V2.0 CURRENT, SE-AI-001 V1.0 CURRENT, SE-AI-002 V1.0 CURRENT, current Registry/S2 machine contracts and actual Forecast/Optimization runtime. No additional route is safe to activate: Registry lacks endpoint-specific create/tree/list projections, Point-centric Telemetry materially differs from current Device-centric S2 contracts, Forecast public route shapes remain recommendation-level, and Optimization runtime is an internal synchronous solver rather than a durable public Run resource. Current adjudication remains A=3, B=0, C=10; those 10 routes stay CONTRACT_NOT_ACTIVE until exact public machine contracts are frozen.

ADR 0012 and contracts/architecture/edge-control-plane.v1.json are now the target for controllable HVAC Edge. Existing EG8200/MQTT/store-forward and command safety are foundations only; Process Image, IPO Cycle, Controller/Scheduler/Arbiter, Capability Profiles, Device Drivers/Protocol Bridges, Edge Manifest, Edge Timedata and leased remote intents are not yet complete.

Phase1 default business deployables converge to energy-api + iot-service + telemetry-worker + metric-worker. Scheduler and Maintenance are supporting application workloads rather than new business deployables; Identity remains separate infrastructure. Logical owner TLS/SPIFFE boundaries remain intact inside energy-api, iot-service retains separate dispatch/verification credentials, telemetry-worker owns history and analytics projections, and metric-worker performs explicit scheduled finalization plus scoped cross-store reconciliation. Forecast, Optimization and FDD remain optional selective intelligence services.

Phase1 deploys platform-owned identity-service as non-business Identity Infrastructure. It owns credentials and standard OIDC authentication only; platform IAM remains the authorization source of truth for Tenant, Site, Role and Policy.

Object Storage governance and a provider-neutral external Phase1 binding contract are now deployed without selecting a product. V2.1.2 does not freeze a vendor, so PASS still requires a real production endpoint, credential reference and governed bucket catalog to be provisioned by deployment.
